scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF
from each other!! From the department head's machine (it_hod) none of the CS
computers (the 192.168.2.x ones) answer any more -- our own department is
fine, it's just CS that's gone. The router that joins the two departments has
obviously dropped one of its sides -- it's still talking to us but it has let
go of CS, one hundred percent!! Please plug the CS side back into the router
and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The IT–CS interdepartment path is currently healthy. From the IT HOD’s machine (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) we can reach every CS host: cs_hod (192.168.2.2) and cs_lab1–cs_lab4 (192.168.2.3–.6) all respond with 0% loss and low RTTs. In the reverse direction, CS can reach IT as well (e.g., cs_hod to it_lab1/it_lab4 both succeed). The router alleged to have “dropped the CS side” (router0) has both departmental interfaces up and forwarding: eth0 192.168.1.1/24 and eth1 192.168.2.1/24 show UP/LOWER_UP with no errors/drops, and the routing table contains directly connected routes for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24. Default gateways on hosts are correct (it_hod via 192.168.1.1, cs_hod via 192.168.2.1).

Mechanism-wise, if router0 had lost its CS-facing link, L3 pings from 192.168.1.0/24 to any 192.168.2.x would fail consistently, and router0’s eth1 would be DOWN or missing the connected route. None of that is observed.

Localization: No fault found on router0 (eth0/eth1), IT LAN, CS LAN, or their L2 segments via switch0/switch1. All tested paths operate as expected.

Root cause: No current defect; the outage was either transient and has self-cleared, or the initial report was a false alarm.

Corrective fix: No action required. Recommend monitoring for intermittents (e.g., continuous ping from it_hod to 192.168.2.2), and, if symptoms reappear, capture interface counters/ethtool on router0 eth1 and switch1 ports to pinpoint a flapping link.
